```suggestion
The term "Technical Steering Committee" (TSC) describes the group of Kedro maintainers, committers, and advisors. We list Kedro's [current](#current-kedro-tsc-members) and [past](#past-kedro-tsc-members) TSC members on this page.

I'm sorry, I should have brought this up earlier, but I hope it's minor enough to consider. In terms of terminology, I think it would be better to stay with maintainers and committers instead of voting members and committers. My reasoning is two-fold:

- I think it's more standard in the open-source community. If you have some examples where the structure is "voting members" and "maintainers", happy to learn/reconsider; otherwise, I think "maintainers" and "committers" is much more widely understood.
- If the plan/expectations is to retain most people as maintainers, this creates less role churn.

Nit: I also think it's unnecessary to denote past "TSC members and maintainers"; just calling them past "TSC members" to be consistent and more concise is probably fine. Even from the subheading, you could consider dropping "Kedro"; it's pretty obvious we wouldn't be documenting another project TSC.
